notes.text: The opening continuation says the fundamental groups are “en apparence” trivial and displays pi_1 of the indicated topos as zero for 0 <= nu <= 3. En apparence is an addition above triviaux. The upper bound is a heavily retraced 3; the image does not securely recover a separate earlier numeral, so none is supplied. This account does not prove the displayed assertion.

The corrected description says the topos for nu >= 4 corresponds to the scheme of systems of nu-3 distinct points in the displayed punctured line. The canceled est le gros topos fibré and étale de are retained, together with the interlinear additions. The right-hand geometric letter in the display is E with a doubled left stroke, and is reproduced as E rather than replaced by a mathematically expected letter.

The author adds that the fundamental group is the profinite completion of a braid group, then says that this group, “en tant que” a “groupe extérieur”, depends contravariantly on the indicated interval for monomorphisms. En tant que and extérieur are source words omitted or left unread in H. No braid-group presentation or functoriality claim has been proved in this reading.

The final paragraph describes the symmetric-group action and the product action with Gamma. The interlinear word is du, not donc; the unusual wording is left unchanged. Du and the barred-Q topos expression are kept as one addition before on fait opérer, following their continuous interlinear placement and H's order. The tiny comma in that inserted index remains genuinely uncertain, and the paragraph ends with the source comma.

Five opaque black marks below the final paragraph are reproduced as physical shapes, without asserting that they form an intentional mathematical drawing or that they are in the author's hand. The pencil numerals 14 and 27 are assigned to an unnamed hand. H's appended conjecture heading, underline and reported circled 9 are absent from this sheet; no other sheet was consulted to relocate them.

All five topos letters retain the shared C/H mathcal T encoding. Their shape resembles the round object-set glyph encountered in the shared notation table, but the distinct topos notation is not conflated with it. Bold versus blackboard font choices for the field/geometric letters are treated as renderings of the same visible double-stroke convention, not new mathematical symbols.

Local coordinate check: for an ordered configuration of nu distinct points of a projective line with nu >= 3, the unique fractional-linear change sending three chosen labeled points to infinity, 0 and 1 leaves nu-3 mutually distinct coordinates in the complement of those three points. For nu=3 no coordinates remain; for nu=4 one coordinate remains in that complement. This verifies the local count and the punctured-line expression in the corrected description, conditional on labeled markings. It neither proves the topos equivalence or the fundamental-group assertions nor changes the manuscript letter E to another convention.

raw_difference_disposition: All 28 packet differences were checked against the original and both existing native halves, including every agreed source word, formula, index, quote mark, cancellation, insertion and numeral. Differences 1–2 are scan/page-note formatting; the visible pencil 14 is retained. Difference 3 concerns en apparence and is covered with H's incorrect known-word note in difference 9. Differences 4–5 and 8 are real punctuation differences; 6–7 and 11 are leq/leqslant or geq/geqslant macro choices, with both lower bars verified in the ink. Differences 9–13 concern Topos and the layered corrected description and are covered by separate word/state rows. Difference 14 is the horizontal subtraction sign. Difference 15 is H's editorial note about double-stroked E; the source E is retained, and C-style bold versus H blackboard fonts are treated as rendering conventions. Difference 16 is the macro boundary at d' plus un, not a changed word; its insertion state is recorded separately. Differences 17–18 are the missing en tant que, quote forms and extérieur. Differences 19–21 concern the complete interlinear du-expression placement. Differences 22–28 are contaminated by comparison of C's figure code with H's editorial note and appended heading; the five physical marks, absent heading and bottom numeral are explicitly accounted for. No circled 9 or conjecture title appears on this sheet. All eight unique crops were emitted and inspected; no OCR, web research, TeX compilation or audit of other pages was performed.
